questions.question: Which body recommends the distribution of taxes between Center and States?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Finance Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Finance Commission** is a **constitutional body** established by the **President of India** under **Article 280** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• Its primary mandate is to define the financial relations between the **Central Government** and the **State Governments**, ensuring a balanced distribution of resources.
 
• The commission provides critical recommendations on the **distribution of net proceeds of taxes** between the Union and the States, a process known as **vertical devolution**.
 
• It also determines the principles for **horizontal devolution**, which is the allocation of tax proceeds among the various **State Governments** based on specific criteria like population, area, and fiscal capacity.
 
• Furthermore, it specifies the principles governing **grants-in-aid** to the States from the **Consolidated Fund of India** under **Article 275**.
 
• The **First Finance Commission** was constituted in **1951** under the chairmanship of **K.C. Neogy**, and typically, a new commission is formed every **five years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NITI Aayog**:

 
 
• Established on **January 1, 2015**, it replaced the erstwhile **Planning Commission**.
 
• It serves as the **premier policy think-tank** of the Government of India, fostering **cooperative federalism** through a bottom-up approach.
 
• Unlike the Finance Commission, it does not possess the power to allocate or distribute funds to state governments.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission**:
 
 
• Formed in **1950** as a **non-constitutional** and **non-statutory body** to formulate **Five-Year Plans**.
 
• It was responsible for central planning and resource allocation before being dissolved in **2014**.
 
 
 
• **Parliament**:
 
 
• The **supreme legislative body** of India, comprising the **President**, **Lok Sabha**, and **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• It holds the authority to enact laws and pass the **Union Budget**, but it relies on the technical recommendations of the **Finance Commission** for tax sharing mechanisms.

questions.question: Who appoints the chairman and members of the Finance Commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Finance Commission** is a **quasi-judicial** and **constitutional body** established by the **President** of India under **Article 280** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• According to **Article 280(1)**, the **President** is responsible for constituting the commission every **five years** or at such earlier time as he or she considers necessary.
 
• The commission consists of a **Chairman** and **four other members**, all of whom are officially appointed by the **President** by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• The **Chairman** must be a person having experience in **public affairs**, while the other members are selected from among people who are **High Court judges**, have specialized knowledge of **finance and accounts**, or have wide experience in **financial matters** and **economics**.
 
• The primary function of the body is to provide recommendations to the **President** regarding the **distribution of tax proceeds** between the **Union** and the **States** and the principles governing **grants-in-aid**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliamentary Role**:

 
 
• While the **President** appoints the members, **Article 280(2)** grants **Parliament** the power to determine the **qualifications** and the **manner of selection** of the members.
 
• This led to the enactment of the **Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951**, which defines the eligibility criteria for the **Chairman** and members.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• The **First Finance Commission** was established in **1951** under the chairmanship of **K.C. Neogy**.
 
• The **15th Finance Commission** was chaired by **N.K. Singh**, and its recommendations cover the period up to **2025-26**.
 
• The **16th Finance Commission** has recently been constituted with **Arvind Panagariya** as its **Chairman**.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Mechanism**:
 
 
• Under **Article 281**, the **President** must lay the recommendations of the **Finance Commission**, along with an **explanatory memorandum** on the action taken, before each **House of Parliament**.

questions.question: During which festival is Gaur dance predominantly performed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Holi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gaur dance** is a world-renowned tribal folk dance performed by the **Bison Horn Maria** tribe, who primarily reside in the **Bastar** district of **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• This dance is predominantly performed during the spring festival of **Holi** (also known as **Phagun**) to celebrate the bounty of nature and the community's hunting traditions.
 
• The name of the dance is derived from the **Gaur** (Indian Bison), which is considered a symbol of strength and vitality by the tribe.
 
• Male performers wear a magnificent headdress made of **bison horns**, decorated with tufts of feathers and cowrie shells, mimicking the movements and spirit of a charging bull.
 
• The dance is characterized by energetic movements, rhythmic footwork, and the thunderous sound of large **Dhol** drums, which represent the heartbeat of the forest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maria Tribe**:

 
 
• They are a major sub-group of the **Gond** community and are known for their distinct **Ghotul** system and rich artistic heritage.
 
• The **Bison Horn Maria** are specifically distinguished by their unique ritualistic use of animal horns in ceremonies.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Other Festivals**:
 
 
• **Diwali**: Known as the festival of lights, it is a pan-Indian festival but is not the primary occasion for the traditional **Gaur dance**.
 
• **Navratri**: This nine-night festival is dedicated to the **Goddess Durga** and is more famous for the **Garba** and **Dandiya** dances in **Gujarat**.
 
• **Baisakhi**: It is a major harvest and religious festival celebrated in **Punjab** and **Haryana**, marking the formation of the **Khalsa Panth** in **1699**.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Instruments**: The performance relies heavily on traditional instruments like the **Mandri**, **Tirududi** (musical sticks), and brass flutes to maintain a high-energy tempo throughout the night.

questions.question: Which Sikh scripture is recited during Hola Mohalla?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guru Granth Sahib**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hola Mohalla** is a prominent **Sikh festival** celebrated annually, typically in the month of **March**, one day after the Hindu festival of **Holi**.
 
• The festival was initiated by the tenth Sikh Guru, **Guru Gobind Singh**, in **1701** at **Anandpur Sahib** to transform the peaceful celebration of Holi into a display of **martial spirit** and military prowess.
 
• The **Guru Granth Sahib**, the central religious scripture of **Sikhism**, is the focal point of the celebrations; its verses are recited through **Akhand Path** (continuous reading) and **Kirtan** (devotional singing) throughout the event.
 
• During the festivities, **Nihang Sikhs** perform traditional martial arts known as **Gatka**, engage in mock battles, and demonstrate equestrian skills, all while maintaining the spiritual atmosphere through the recitation of **Gurbani**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru Granth Sahib**:

 
 
• It was first compiled as the **Adi Granth** by the fifth Guru, **Guru Arjan Dev**, in **1604** and later finalized by **Guru Gobind Singh**, who designated it as the eternal Guru.
 
• It contains **1,430 pages** (Angs) and includes the teachings of six Sikh Gurus and various medieval saints like **Kabir** and **Baba Farid**.
 
 
 
• **Bhagavad Gita**:
 
 
• A sacred **Hindu** scripture consisting of **700 verses**, it forms a part of the Indian epic **Mahabharata** and features a dialogue between **Lord Krishna** and **Arjuna**.
 
 
 
• **Quran**:
 
 
• The central religious text of **Islam**, believed by Muslims to be the verbatim word of **God (Allah)** as revealed to the **Prophet Muhammad**.
 
 
 
• **Bible**:
 
 
• The holy scripture of **Christianity**, comprised of the **Old Testament** and the **New Testament**, detailing the history of the faith and the life of **Jesus Christ**.

questions.question: When is acceleration considered positive?

options.text: When it is opposite to velocity
When it is in the direction of velocity
When the object is at rest

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When it is in the direction of velocity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the rate at which an object changes its **velocity**. It is a **vector quantity**, meaning it possesses both magnitude and direction.
 
• The standard unit for measuring acceleration is meters per second squared (**m/s²**).
 
• Acceleration is considered **positive** when the change in velocity occurs in the same direction as the motion of the object. This typically results in the object **speeding up**.
 
• Mathematically, if the **final velocity** (v) is greater than the **initial velocity** (u) over a time period (t), the acceleration (a = (v − u) / t) yields a positive value.
 
• When the **acceleration vector** and the **velocity vector** point in the same direction, the magnitude of the velocity increases, confirming a positive acceleration relative to the direction of travel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Negative Acceleration (Retardation)**:

 
 
• This occurs when the acceleration acts in the **opposite direction** to the velocity of the object.
 
• In such cases, the object **slows down** or undergoes **deceleration**. For example, applying brakes to a moving car produces negative acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Zero Acceleration**:
 
 
• An object has zero acceleration when it is **at rest** or moving with a **constant velocity** in a straight line.
 
• If there is no change in **speed** or **direction**, the acceleration is null.
 
 
 
• **Directional Sign Conventions**:
 
 
• The sign of acceleration (+ or −) depends on the chosen **coordinate system**.
 
• An object moving in a **negative direction** (e.g., left) that is slowing down actually has **positive acceleration** because the acceleration vector points in the positive direction (right) to oppose the motion.

questions.question: Frankenstein is written by ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mary Shelley**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mary Shelley** was an **English novelist** who wrote the iconic novel **Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus**, which was first published in **1818**.
 
• The novel is frequently categorized as a masterpiece of **Gothic horror** and is widely regarded by scholars as the first true work of **science fiction**.
 
• The story was famously conceived during a competition to write ghost stories in **1816** at **Villa Diodati** in **Switzerland**, where Mary was staying with **Percy Bysshe Shelley** and **Lord Byron**.
 
• The plot centers on **Victor Frankenstein**, a scientist who animates a creature made from scavenged body parts, leading to an exploration of **scientific responsibility** and **existential despair**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bram Stoker**

 
 
• An **Irish author** celebrated for his **1897** Gothic novel **Dracula**, which significantly shaped the modern **vampire** mythology in literature and film.
 
 
 
• **H.G. Wells**
 
 
• An **English writer** known as one of the 'fathers of science fiction' for his visionary works including **The Time Machine (1895)**, **The Invisible Man (1897)**, and **The War of the Worlds (1898)**.
 
 
 
• **Robert Louis Stevenson**
 
 
• A **Scottish novelist** and poet famous for his psychological thriller **Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde (1886)** and the adventure classic **Treasure Island (1883)**.

questions.question: The Ease of Doing Business (EODB) indicator "Enforcing Contracts" measures:

options.text: Ease of paying and managing taxes
Efficiency of the judicial system in resolving commercial disputes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Efficiency of the judicial system in resolving commercial disputes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Enforcing Contracts** indicator is a core component of the **World Bank Group**'s **Ease of Doing Business (EODB)** index, which evaluates the efficiency of the **judicial system** in handling commercial litigation.
 
• It measures the **time** and **cost** for resolving a commercial dispute through a local first-instance court, based on a standardized case study of a **sales contract dispute** between two domestic businesses.
 
• The **Time** metric calculates the duration in calendar days from the moment the plaintiff files the lawsuit until the final **enforcement of judgment** or actual payment.
 
• The **Cost** metric is expressed as a percentage of the **claim value** and includes court fees, **attorney fees**, and enforcement costs required to complete the litigation process.
 
• It also features a **Quality of Judicial Processes Index**, which uses a **0-18 scale** to assess court structure, **case management**, court automation, and the availability of **Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR)**.
 
• A high ranking indicates that an economy has a **transparent**, predictable, and **efficient legal framework**, which reduces uncertainty and risks for entrepreneurs and investors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other key indicators within the **Doing Business** framework include:

 
 
• **Paying Taxes**: Measures the **total tax rate**, time taken to comply with tax laws, and the complexity of **post-filing processes** like audits or refunds.
 
• **Labor Market Regulation**: Analyzes the flexibility of **employment contracts**, including regulations on hiring, working hours, and **severance pay**.
 
• **Resolving Insolvency**: Focuses on the efficiency and outcome of **bankruptcy proceedings**, measuring recovery rates and the **strength of the insolvency framework**.
 
• **Registering Property**: Tracks the number of procedures, time, and cost involved in transferring a **land title** from one company to another.
 
 
 
• In **2021**, the World Bank announced the discontinuation of the **Doing Business** report, replacing it with a more comprehensive project titled **Business Ready (B-READY)**.

questions.question: In which city and year were the first World Athletics Championships held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Helsinki, 1983**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The inaugural **World Athletics Championships** were held in **Helsinki**, **Finland**, between **August 7 and August 14, 1983**.
 
• The event was organized by the **International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF)**, which is now known as **World Athletics**.
 
• The primary venue for the competition was the **Helsinki Olympic Stadium**, which had previously hosted the **1952 Summer Olympics**.
 
• This championship marked a significant shift in track and field history, as it was the first time a standalone global competition was conducted independently of the **Olympic Games**.
 
• A total of **1,333 athletes** from **153 nations** participated, competing across **41 sports events**, including 24 for men and 17 for women.
 
• The **United States** emerged as the most successful nation in terms of the medal tally, securing **24 medals**, including **8 golds**, with the **Soviet Union** and **East Germany** following closely.
 
• American sprinter and long jumper **Carl Lewis** was the standout athlete of the meet, winning **three gold medals** in the **100 meters**, **long jump**, and the **4×100 meters relay**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The World Athletics Championships followed a **quadrennial cycle** (every four years) until 1991, after which it transitioned to a **biennial cycle** (every two years).
 
• **Rome, 1987**:
 
 
• This was the **second edition** of the championships held at the **Stadio Olimpico** in **Italy**.
 
• It featured **43 events** and saw the introduction of the **10,000 meters** and **10 km walk** for women.
 
 
 
• **Tokyo, 1991**:
 
 
• The **third edition** was hosted in **Japan** and is widely remembered for **Mike Powell** breaking **Bob Beamon's** long-standing **long jump world record** with a leap of **8.95 meters**.
 
 
 
• **Stuttgart, 1993**:
 
 
• The **fourth edition** took place in **Germany** (the option mentions **Berlin**, but the 1993 event was actually in **Stuttgart**).
 
• It was the first championship where the **biennial schedule** was fully implemented.

questions.concept: Origin and evolution of Universe Solar system
questions.question: If a spacecraft travels at 30 km/s, how long will it take to cover 1 AU (150 million km)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**58 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To find the time taken for the journey, we use the fundamental kinematic formula: **Time = Distance ÷ Speed**.
 
• The distance to be covered is **1 Astronomical Unit (AU)**, which is defined as approximately **150,000,000 kilometers**.
 
• The constant speed of the spacecraft is provided as **30 km/s**.
 
• First, calculate the total time in seconds: **150,000,000 km ÷ 30 km/s = 5,000,000 seconds**.
 
• To convert this duration into a more standard unit like days, we determine the number of seconds in one day: **24 hours × 60 minutes × 60 seconds = 86,400 seconds**.
 
• Finally, divide the total seconds by the seconds per day: **5,000,000 ÷ 86,400 ≈ 57.87 days**.
 
• When rounded to the nearest whole number, the duration equals **58 days**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Astronomical Unit (AU)**

 
 
• It serves as a standard unit of measurement in **astronomy** to describe distances within the **Solar System**.
 
• It represents the **mean distance** between the center of the **Earth** and the center of the **Sun**, approximately **93 million miles**.
 
 
 
• **Relative Speeds in Space**
 
 
• A speed of **30 km/s** is comparable to the **orbital velocity of Earth**, which moves at about **29.78 km/s** around the Sun.
 
• In comparison, **light** travels at **299,792 km/s**, meaning it takes only about **8 minutes and 20 seconds** for sunlight to reach Earth.
 
• Man-made probes like the **Voyager 1** travel at roughly **17 km/s**, whereas the **Parker Solar Probe** has reached record-breaking speeds exceeding **150 km/s** during its solar approach.

questions.question: In which year did India take over the BRICS Chairship from Russia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India officially assumed the **BRICS Chairship** from the **Russian Federation** on **January 1, 2021**.
 
• The year **2021** marked the **third time** India headed the group, after previously holding the presidency in **2012** and **2016**.
 
• Under its chairship, India hosted the **13th BRICS Summit** on **September 9, 2021**, which was chaired by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** in a virtual format.
 
• The chairship of **BRICS** (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa) rotates annually among the members in accordance with the acronym **B-R-I-C-S**; thus, **Russia** handed over the baton to **India**.
 
• The primary theme selected by India for its 2021 tenure was **'BRICS @ 15: Intra-BRICS Cooperation for Continuity, Consolidation and Consensus'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BRICS Formation and Evolution:**

 
 
• The grouping was originally formed as **BRIC** following a meeting of the leaders of **Brazil, Russia, India, and China** in **2006**.
 
• It was expanded to **BRICS** in **2010** with the formal induction of **South Africa** during the **Sanya Summit** in China.
 
• The **BRICS** nations together represent about **41 percent** of the global population, **24 percent** of the global **GDP**, and over **16 percent** of global trade share.
 
• One of the most significant achievements of the group is the establishment of the **New Development Bank (NDB)**, headquartered in **Shanghai**, which was formalized during the **6th BRICS Summit** in **Fortaleza, Brazil (2014)**.
 
• The grouping serves as a platform for **South-South cooperation** and seeks to reform **multilateral institutions** like the **United Nations** and the **IMF** to reflect contemporary global realities.

questions.question: What was the main drawback of small-scale industry reservation policies?

options.text: They restricted economies of scale and technological upgrading

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They restricted economies of scale and technological upgrading**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reservation policy for **Small-Scale Industries (SSIs)** was primarily designed to protect small producers from the competition of large-scale manufacturers and to promote **employment generation**.
 
• A significant drawback was the **investment limit** placed on plant and machinery; firms that expanded their capital beyond a specific threshold lost their **SSI status** and associated government incentives.
 
• This policy created a **perverse incentive** for entrepreneurs to keep their units small, which prevented them from achieving **economies of scale**, leading to higher **marginal costs** of production.
 
• Due to the fear of losing protection, these industries avoided **technological upgrading** and modernization, resulting in **technological obsolescence** and lower productivity compared to global standards.
 
• The lack of scale and modern technology eventually made these units **uncompetitive** in the international market, as they could not match the quality or price of goods produced by large-scale global firms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karve Committee (1955)**:

 
 
• Also known as the **Village and Small-Scale Industries Committee**, it first suggested using small-scale industries as a tool for **rural development** and social justice.
 
 
 
• **Abed Hussain Committee**:
 
 
• This committee later recommended the **de-reservation** of items, arguing that reservation hindered the **export potential** and growth of the manufacturing sector.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution 1956**:
 
 
• It laid the foundation for the **Public Sector** and provided various **fiscal concessions**, like lower excise duties and bank loans at lower interest rates, to the SSI sector.
 
 
 
• **Post-1991 Reforms**:
 
 
• Following **Liberalization**, the government began a phased de-reservation process to allow **Market Competition** to drive efficiency and innovation within the industry.

questions.question: Which was the model for the First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harrod-Domar model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **First Five-Year Plan** was launched for the period of **1951 to 1956** under the leadership of India's first Prime Minister, **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
 
• The plan was based on the **Harrod-Domar model**, which posits that economic growth depends on the **level of savings** and the **capital-output ratio**; specifically, it suggests that higher savings lead to higher investment and thus higher growth.
 
• The primary focus of this plan was the **development of the primary sector**, with a heavy emphasis on **agriculture**, **irrigation**, and **power** to address the food shortages caused by the partition of India.
 
• Significant investments were made in large-scale multipurpose projects, including the **Bhakra-Nangal**, **Hirakud**, and **Damodar Valley** dams, to improve irrigation and power generation.
 
• The plan was highly successful, achieving a **growth rate of 3.6%**, which significantly exceeded the target growth rate of **2.1%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahalanobis Model**

 
 
• Formulated by statistician **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**, this model served as the blueprint for the **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)**.
 
• It shifted the economic focus from agriculture to **rapid industrialization**, specifically emphasizing **heavy and basic industries** like steel and chemicals.
 
 
 
• **Solow Model**
 
 
• Developed by **Robert Solow**, this is an **exogenous growth model** that analyzes long-run economic growth by looking at **capital accumulation**, **labor growth**, and **technological progress**.
 
• Unlike the Harrod-Domar model, it accounts for **diminishing returns** to capital and emphasizes that **technological change** is the ultimate driver of growth.
 
 
 
• **Keynesian Model**
 
 
• Originating from **John Maynard Keynes**, this macroeconomic theory focuses on how **aggregate demand** (total spending) influences output and inflation.
 
• It advocates for **government intervention** through fiscal and monetary policies to manage economic cycles, particularly to mitigate **recessions** and **unemployment**.

questions.question: What is the length of a standard field hockey pitch?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**91.4 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A standard field hockey pitch is a rectangular playing surface with a specific length of **91.40 meters** (equivalent to **100 yards**) and a width of **55.00 meters** (equivalent to **60 yards**).
 
• The dimensions and markings are strictly regulated by the **International Hockey Federation (FIH)**, which is the global governing body for the sport.
 
• The total area of a regulation field is approximately **5,027 square meters**, and it is divided by a **center line** and two **23-meter lines** (historically 25-yard lines).
 
• The pitch is marked with **white lines** that are **75 mm** wide, and these lines are considered part of the playing area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Specific Field Markings:
 
 
• **Shooting Circle (D)**: A semi-circular area formed by two quarter-circles with a radius of **14.63 meters** (16 yards) from the inner front corner of each goal post.
 
• **Penalty Spot**: A circular mark with a diameter of **150 mm**, positioned **6.40 meters** (7 yards) from the center of the goal line.
 
• **Penalty Corner Markings**: Markers are placed on the backline at **5 meters** and **10 meters** from the goal posts to facilitate set plays.
 
 
 
• Playing Surfaces:
 
 
• Modern high-level hockey is played almost exclusively on **artificial turf**, which provides a fast and consistent ball roll.
 
• **Water-based pitches** are the standard for **Olympic Games** and **World Cups**, requiring a layer of water to reduce friction and prevent player injury.
 
• **Sand-dressed** or **sand-filled** artificial grass is commonly used at club and school levels for durability.

questions.question: What is the goal of the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) scheme launched in 2015?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Urban infrastructure and water supply**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT)** was launched by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)** in **June 2015** to improve the quality of life in urban areas.
 
• The primary objective of the mission is to ensure that every household has access to a **functional tap** with an assured supply of water and a **sewerage connection** to manage waste effectively.
 
• It prioritizes the development of **urban infrastructure**, specifically focusing on **stormwater drainage** to reduce flooding and the promotion of **non-motorized urban transport** like cycling and walking.
 
• The mission aims to increase the **amenity value of cities** by developing and maintaining **green spaces**, **parks**, and well-designed **open spaces**, especially for children.
 
• AMRUT covers **500 cities** across India, including those with a population of over **one lakh**, capital cities, and identified heritage cities or cities on the banks of main rivers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **AMRUT 2.0:**

 
 
• Launched in **October 2021**, this subsequent phase aims to make Indian cities **water secure** and provide 100% coverage of water supply to all households in about **4,700 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)**.
 
• It promotes the **circular economy of water** through the development of **City Water Balance Plans** focusing on recycle/reuse of treated sewage and rejuvenation of water bodies.
 
 
 
• **Related Urban Schemes:**
 
 
• **Smart Cities Mission:** Focused on driving economic growth and improving quality of life through **local development** and **technology**.
 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban:** Concentrates on making cities **garbage-free** and **open defecation free (ODF)**.

questions.question: What term was used to describe the student stage of life in early Hindu philosophy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmachari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Brahmachari** identifies a student during the **Brahmacharya** stage, which is the first of the four **Ashramas** (stages of life) in ancient Hindu philosophy.
 
• This stage typically commenced between the ages of 8 and 12 following the **Upanayana** ceremony, which symbolized the initiation into formal **Vedic education**.
 
• A **Brahmachari** resided in a **Gurukula** (teacher's household), where they served the **Guru** and learned various subjects including the **Vedas**, philosophy, grammar, and ethics.
 
• The core values of this stage included strict **celibacy**, **self-discipline**, and the practice of **Bhiksha** (seeking alms) to cultivate a sense of humility and social equality.
 
• The duration of this stage was intended to prepare the individual for their future responsibilities in society by building a strong foundation of **Dharma** (righteousness).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Ashrama system**, or **Chaturashrama**, outlines the progression of human life toward spiritual liberation:

 
 
• **Grihastha**: The second stage (householder), where an individual marries, raises a family, and fulfills social and economic duties through **Artha** (wealth) and **Kama** (desire).
 
• **Vanaprastha**: The third stage (forest-dweller), which begins as one transitions from worldly attachments toward a more secluded, contemplative life of **spiritual study**.
 
• **Sannyasin**: The final stage of **renunciation**, where the individual abandons all material ties and social status to focus entirely on achieving **Moksha** (liberation from birth and death).

questions.question: The PCPNDT Act was enacted by the Government of India in _____ for prohibition of sex selection.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1994**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act** was enacted by the **Parliament of India** in **1994** to provide for the prohibition of sex selection, before or after conception.
 
• The act aims to regulate the use of **pre-natal diagnostic techniques**, such as **ultrasound** and **amniocentesis**, by restricting them to the detection of genetic abnormalities, metabolic disorders, or certain congenital malformations.
 
• The legislation was a critical response to the social menace of **female foeticide** and the rapidly declining **child sex ratio** in India, which was observed during the **1991 Census**.
 
• It mandates that no person, including the specialist conducting the procedure, shall communicate the **sex of the foetus** to the pregnant woman or her relatives by words, signs, or any other method.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution and Implementation:**

 
 
• The Act officially came into force on **January 1, 1996**, and was later amended in **2003** to improve its implementation and encompass **pre-conception sex selection** techniques.
 
• It established the **Central Supervisory Board (CSB)**, chaired by the **Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare**, to advise the Central Government on policy matters.
 
• Under the Act, all **Genetic Counselling Centres**, **Genetic Laboratories**, and **Genetic Clinics** must be registered with the **Appropriate Authority** to operate legally.
 
• Non-compliance or violation of the provisions can result in imprisonment for a term up to **3 years** and a fine up to **10,000 rupees** for the first conviction.

questions.question: To whom did the rebel soldiers of the Meerut Regiment want to hand over the rule of the country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahadur Shah Zafar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **May 10, 1857**, the rebellion began in **Meerut** when sepoys refused to use the new **Enfield rifle** cartridges, leading to a violent breakout against British officers.
 
• The rebel soldiers of the **Meerut Regiment** marched through the night and reached **Delhi** on the morning of **May 11, 1857**, crossing the **Yamuna** river.
 
• The soldiers gathered at the **Red Fort** and demanded to meet **Bahadur Shah Zafar**, the last **Mughal Emperor**, to seek his leadership and blessing for the uprising.
 
• Despite his initial hesitation due to his advanced age of **82 years** and lack of resources, the Emperor was proclaimed **Shahenshah-e-Hindustan** (Emperor of India) by the sepoys.
 
• The choice of **Bahadur Shah Zafar** was symbolic, as the **Mughal Dynasty** still carried historical **legitimacy** across various regions and communities in India, serving as a unifying figure against the **British East India Company**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nana Saheb**

 
 
• He was the adopted son of the late **Peshwa Baji Rao II** and led the rebellion in **Kanpur**.
 
• He declared himself **Peshwa** but notably acknowledged **Bahadur Shah Zafar** as the supreme Emperor of India.
 
 
 
• **Rani Lakshmibai**
 
 
• The Queen of **Jhansi** who joined the rebellion after her kingdom was annexed under the **Doctrine of Lapse**.
 
• She became one of the most formidable leaders of the revolt, fighting alongside **Tantia Tope**.
 
 
 
• **Peshwa Baji Rao II**
 
 
• The last **Peshwa** of the **Maratha Empire** who was exiled to **Bithoor** by the British after the **Third Anglo-Maratha War**.
 
• He passed away in **1851**, several years before the **Revolt of 1857** began.
 
 
 
• **Consequences for the Emperor**
 
 
• After the British recaptured **Delhi** in **September 1857**, the Emperor was tried for treason and exiled to **Rangoon** (Burma), where he died in **1862**.
